verdicts.reason: Same correct unit economics in both; Output 2 adds a projected outcome of the new split, a concrete retargeting/DPA de-overlap and the prepaid-vs-COD lever, while Output 1's headline count (cut two, hold three) contradicts its own table.

Both sound; Output 2 is more Monday-ready with owner and done-when set-up steps, ad-group budgets that add up, concrete wave hooks and creator disclosure rules, though Output 1's blended incrementality read on day 30 is a little stronger.

Output 1 gives truly distinct formats (static, carousel, sound-led, creator) with headlines, safe zones and a keep/cut rule, while Output 2 leans on Reels and its cost-per-trip ad implies durability beyond the approved claims.

Output 1's creator brief covers rights, usage term, dates and deliverables, puts spoken plus on-screen disclosure in the first seconds and guards the blind test against implied claims; Output 2's brief is thinner.
Both count characters correctly and test sensibly; Output 2 adds a brand-name angle, a sharper headline set, a concrete keep/cut rule and the FSSAI and 'sugar-free' caution.
Very close; Output 2 puts a note-count placeholder into the copy, routes cash-heavy shoppers to a full-note wallet instead of losing them, and gives a fallback if conversion drops.

Output 1 is a more expert Klaviyo build (unique expiring codes, checkout pause, exit filter) with a consultative WhatsApp step that tackles the 'which active' doubt, while Output 2 uses a shared static code and a reminder-only WhatsApp.

Output 1 holds offers to message 3, gives full-price buyers a gift instead of a discount, sunsets the over-365 group and handles complaint customers first, with checked value maths; Output 2 discounts older groups from day 0 and trains the list to wait for codes.

Both find the $94 break-even correctly; Output 1 ties every move to the board's contribution-margin target with verified 13.6% to 7.8% maths, while Output 2's stop lines are strong but it leans on an unsupported '300 screen'.

Arithmetic checks out in both; Output 2 adds a flexible Pick Any 2 bundle, cautious and bad-case threshold scenarios, a reason to reject ₹849 and the 'free' ad-code rule, though its pre/post test is weaker than Output 1's split.

Output 2's 2x2 design is efficient, but Output 1 judges every test on orders and gross profit per visitor, waits for COD to settle and checks trial returns, which is safer money logic than shipping add-to-cart wins.

Output 1 sizes the prepaid discount against post-confirmation RTO, keeps COD claims pincode-true, adds a missed-delivery template and call capacity maths; Output 2 promises COD in every cart message and suggests a prepaid nudge could go as Utility.
